title: Use of Different Devices or Cards when Entering and Exiting Buses and MRTs, and Claims for Refunds
what_it_is: Use of Different Devices or Cards when Entering and Exiting Buses and MRTs, and Claims for Refunds

sections.label: Refunds for mismatched device taps
sections.summary: Two in 100,000 trips got refunds averaging $2.70 because different devices or cards were used at entry and exit, and automatic reconciliation is not possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The usage of different devices or cards at entry and exit led to refunds for two out of every 100,000 trips made on public transport, with each refund amounting to $2.70 on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is not possible to identify and reconcile such transactions automatically, since a single card can be used by different commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For example, the same bank card can be set up on multiple devices for use by different family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is also presently not operationally feasible to stop commuters who are using SimplyGo from exiting if they use a different device or card from the one used at entry, as this would require a check with the backend system, which will slow down the flow of commuters and lead to long queues during peak hours.

sections.label: SimplyGo publicity on same card
sections.summary: Since the March 2017 Mastercard SimplyGo pilot, publicity has reminded commuters to use the same card or device to enter and exit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Similarly, since the Mastercard pilot for SimplyGo started in March 2017, we have carried out publicity efforts to remind commuters to use the same card or device to enter and exit, such as by placing posters at fare gates and on buses, putting up outdoor banners, making in-station announcements, using radio advertisements, as well as publicising on the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and SimplyGo websites and social media platforms.

sections.label: Charges for missing rail and bus taps
sections.summary: Missing rail entries or exits are charged $2.30 each, and bus fares use maximum possible distance when a tap record is missing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For rail, if there is a missing entry or a missing exit, that means when you tap in with a different card, it will record as two separate transactions with a missing entry and a missing exit, each one will be charged at $2.30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If there is a missing entry, for example, you will look at distance from the first bus stop to where you exit, because there is a missing entry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If there is a missing exit tapping, it will look at distance from the point of entry to the end of the bus route.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is because there is no record to calculate the actual distance, so they use the maximum possible distance to compute.
